name: Superior colliculus
summary: The upper pair of bumps on the tectum, a layered structure that maps the visual field and directs the eyes and head toward things of interest. Its superficial layers receive direct retinal and visual cortical input; its deep layers integrate auditory and somatosensory maps and send tectospinal, tectobulbar and tecto-reticular fibers that drive saccades and orienting movements. It lies next to the pretectal area and the posterior commissure, so tumors or hydrocephalus pressing on the dorsal midbrain combine up-gaze palsy with pupillary light-near dissociation.

anatomy.location: Dorsal midbrain forming the rostral half of the tectum, behind the aqueduct and periaqueductal gray, below the pineal gland and the posterior commissure; the brachium of the superior colliculus links it to the lateral geniculate body.

subdivisions.name: Superficial layers
subdivisions.note: retinotopic visual map from the retina and striate cortex

subdivisions.name: Intermediate and deep layers
subdivisions.note: multisensory motor map; saccade and head-turn commands to the PPRF, riMLF and spinal cord

function: Visual grasp reflex: orients eyes and head to novel stimuli; contributes to saccade generation and to blinking and avoidance responses to visual threat.

bestView.label: rostral tectal plate behind the aqueduct
superior colliculus above the inferior colliculus, under the pineal

imaging.normalAppearance: The colliculi form the posterior surface of the midbrain on sagittal T1 as two stacked bumps; the superior colliculus is the upper one, just below the pineal. Flattening of the tectum by hydrocephalus is best seen on sagittal images.

pathology.finding: Bulbous T2-bright enlargement of the tectal plate compressing the aqueduct with hydrocephalus; often non-enhancing and indolent.

pathology.pathology: Pineal region tumor with dorsal midbrain compression
pathology.finding: Mass in the pineal region flattening the superior colliculi and posterior commissure; Parinaud syndrome.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: Sagittal T2/T1 of the tectum and pineal region; look for aqueductal obstruction

lesionEffects.mechanism: Compression of the posterior commissure and adjacent pretectum (dorsal midbrain syndrome)

lesionEffects.deficit: Impaired visual orienting and saccades to the opposite side
lesionEffects.mechanism: Loss of the collicular motor map

examination: Vertical saccades and pursuit; look for lid retraction and convergence-retraction nystagmus on attempted up-gaze
Pupil reactions to light and near
Test saccades to sudden peripheral targets
pearls: Up-gaze palsy in a young person with headache: think pineal tumor or hydrocephalus pressing on the tectum
Isolated colliculus lesions are rare; the syndrome you see is the dorsal midbrain (Parinaud) complex
